robot.name: Figure 01
robot.status_notes: Figure's current company page frames F.01 as the first-generation robot; later customer-confirmed BMW production evidence is Figure 02-specific.

battery.notes: Archived official page listed an electric system but did not provide battery capacity.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Public sources reviewed did not provide total robot degrees of freedom.

hands.description: OpenAI-demo reporting described learned behaviors outputting wrist and finger actions across a 24-DoF action space; no public Figure 01 hand hardware DoF spec was found.

actuators.description: Archived official page described an electric system; actuator details were not found.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Figure 01 demos showed object handling, coffee preparation behavior, and simple task execution in controlled settings.
caveats: No customer-confirmed Figure 01 manipulation deployment was found.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Company demos and media reports show narrow tasks such as coffee making after training and responding to spoken prompts.
caveats: Autonomy limits, retries, and intervention rates were not disclosed.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Public walking demo coverage shows Figure 01 taking biped steps in a controlled environment.
caveats: No independent mobility benchmark or rough-terrain evidence found.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: The OpenAI-integrated demo reported visual scene interpretation and task planning from user prompts.
caveats: Company demo reported by media, not independent benchmark testing.

human_interaction.summary: The OpenAI speech-to-speech demo showed Figure 01 conversing with a person and selecting actions from the scene.
caveats: Reliability across unconstrained conversations was not independently tested.

endurance_reliability.summary: Archived official specs listed 5 hours of runtime, but no public reliability or fleet-operation data was found for Figure 01.
caveats: Runtime is an official spec claim.

human_environment_fit.summary: Figure 01 was human-sized and intended for human-designed workplaces; demos were in controlled human-scale spaces.
caveats: No Figure 01 customer site evidence was found.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Figure signed a BMW agreement while Figure 01 was public, but current Figure and BMW production evidence specifically identifies Figure 02, not Figure 01.
caveats: Do not credit Figure 01 with Figure 02 BMW production metrics.
No public price, purchase path, or research-platform availability found.

evidence_items.title: Archived official Figure 01 specifications
evidence_items.claim: An archived official Figure page listed Figure 01 at 5 ft 6 in, 60 kg, 20 kg payload, 5 hours runtime, 1.2 m/s speed, and electric power.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides core physical and endurance specs.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Archived official product page showed the listed dimensions, payload, runtime, speed, and electric system.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Normalized height from 5 ft 6 in to 167.6 cm; original value preserved.

evidence_items.title: Walking demo coverage
evidence_items.claim: Public coverage of Figure 01 showed the robot walking in a controlled setting after Figure reported first steps in 2023.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Secondary coverage describes the public walking demo and first-steps milestone.
evidence_items.source_location: New Atlas article covering Figure walking demo
evidence_items.verification_notes: Observable walking only; no speed, terrain, stability, or endurance metric.

evidence_items.title: Coffee-making learning demo
evidence_items.claim: Public demo material showed Figure 01 interacting with a coffee-machine task setup in a controlled setting.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows manipulation and learned task execution.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Public demo material showed Figure 01 interacting with a coffee-machine task setup.
evidence_items.source_location: Official Figure LinkedIn demo post and Live Science coverage
evidence_items.verification_notes: Observable coffee-machine interaction separated from the company claim about AI training.

evidence_items.title: Real-world task demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure published a Figure 01 real-world task video showing controlled object manipulation and task behavior.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official real-world task video showed controlled object manipulation behavior.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No repeatability, failure, or intervention-rate data found.

evidence_items.title: OpenAI speech-to-speech interaction demo
evidence_items.claim: Public demo coverage showed Figure 01 conversing with a person and performing simple visible actions in a controlled setting.
evidence_items.notes: Media report of a public company demo.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Public demo coverage showed speech interaction and simple scene-grounded action.
evidence_items.source_location: The Decoder coverage of Figure/OpenAI demo
evidence_items.verification_notes: Visible interaction separated from claims about internal planning or model architecture.

evidence_items.title: BMW agreement was not Figure 01 deployment proof
evidence_items.claim: Figure announced a BMW manufacturing agreement while Figure 01 was public, but later Figure and BMW production evidence identifies Figure 02 in the BMW trial/deployment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Current Figure and BMW production evidence identifies the BMW robot as Figure 02, not Figure 01.
evidence_items.source_location: Figure BMW agreement release; BMW Spartanburg release; Figure production-at-BMW writeup; BMW 2026 Physical AI release
evidence_items.verification_notes: Anti-misattribution item; prevents crediting Figure 01 with Figure 02 deployment metrics such as hours, parts, shifts, or X3 production.

evidence_items.title: Company claim that coffee behavior followed AI training
evidence_items.claim: Figure claimed the coffee-machine behavior followed AI training; this is treated separately from the observable demo.
evidence_items.notes: Company claim about training/autonomy, not independently verified.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents over-crediting a visible demo as verified autonomous learning.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official Figure social post framed the coffee behavior as AI-trained.
evidence_items.source_location: Figure LinkedIn coffee demo post text
evidence_items.verification_notes: Use only as company claim about training; observable action is in a separate Tier 2 item.

evidence_items.title: Reported OpenAI demo control-stack details
evidence_items.claim: Media coverage described the Figure/OpenAI demo as involving speech, vision, planning, and learned visuomotor behaviors, including a reported 10 Hz camera input rate and 200 Hz action generation over a 24-DoF wrist/finger action space.
evidence_items.notes: Internal model behavior and rates are reported, not independently benchmarked.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Adds technical context for the visible language-grounded manipulation demo while keeping it below benchmark or deployment evidence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The article summarized the demo as chat, vision, planning, and task performance, with reported camera and action-generation rates.
evidence_items.source_location: The Decoder article body and technical demo summary
evidence_items.verification_notes: Treat as secondary reporting of Figure/OpenAI technical claims; do not convert the 24-DoF action-space detail into a confirmed hardware hand DoF spec.

evidence_items.title: Current Figure BMW metrics are Figure 02-specific
evidence_items.claim: Figure's current BMW production writeup attributes the 10-hour shifts, 90,000+ loaded parts, 1,250+ runtime hours, 30,000+ X3 contribution, and retirement learnings to Figure 02, not Figure 01.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents Figure 01 from inheriting later BMW deployment proof.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Figure and BMW both identify the production/pilot robot as Figure 02 for the BMW metrics.
evidence_items.source_location: Figure production-at-BMW news page and BMW 2026 Physical AI press release
evidence_items.verification_notes: Use these metrics only for Figure 02; Figure 01 remains without customer-confirmed deployment metrics.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Figure 01 has useful early demo evidence but no Figure 01-specific customer deployment. Keep it separate from Figure 02's BMW metrics.
strongest_positive_evidence: Walking, coffee, and speech-grounded action demos.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No detailed hand, sensor, compute, battery, or total DoF specs.
conflicting_claims: BMW agreement happened during the Figure 01 period, but BMW production evidence is Figure 02-specific.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit Figure 01 with BMW Figure 02 production hours or output.
Do not treat demos as sustained deployment.
Do not infer current availability from archived specs.

currentness.currentness_notes: Evidence should be interpreted historically; Figure 01 is not treated as a current product or deployment platform unless new evidence appears.

excluded_claims.reason: No public purchase path or current product page for Figure 01 was found.
The OpenAI demo shows interaction, but internal planning/model details are not independently verified.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Figure 01 is a superseded first-generation Figure prototype with useful early demos for walking, coffee-machine interaction, and speech-grounded action, but no customer-confirmed deployment. Do not credit it with BMW production metrics, which belong to Figure 02.
strongest_evidence: Controlled public walking and manipulation demos.
weakest_evidence: No detailed sensor, hand, compute, or battery spec.
known_do_not_credit: Verified internal autonomy beyond visible demos.
